lessons.title: Spill ranges, # and @
lessons.mac:
Dynamic arrays need Microsoft 365 (or Excel 2021+) on Mac.
In Excel 2019 the same formula returns one value, or needs ⌘ + Shift + Return to enter as an old array formula.

steps.say: One formula in E2 works out the revenue for all ten products. The results spill down by themselves, and the total in G2 refers to the whole spill with a hash sign, so it stays right if the list grows.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. One formula, many results: the spill range
2. The # spill reference
3. Fixing #SPILL! and what @ means

Practice sheet: S09-01

steps.say: In Microsoft 365, a formula that returns several values spills them into the cells below or to the right. Only the first cell holds the formula. The rest are shown in grey in the formula bar and can't be edited.

acts.t:
Dynamic arrays
=B2:B11*C2:C11   ten results from one formula
E2#   the whole spill range that starts in E2
#SPILL!   something is blocking the cells the result needs
@   'just one value': the one in the same row (implicit intersection)

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Units in column B and price in column C.
In E2, type equals, then select B2 to B11 by typing it, a star, and C2 to C11. Press Return.
Ten answers from one formula. Click E5. The formula bar shows it in grey, because it lives in E2. The blue border marks the spill range.
Now total it. In G2, type equals SUM, open bracket, E2, then a hash sign. Close and press Return. E2 hash means the entire spill, however many rows it has.
Here's the common mistake. Someone types a note in E6. Type the word check there and press Return.
E2 shows hash SPILL, and the total breaks too. The formula needs E2 to E11 empty, and E6 is in the way. Click E2 to see the dashed border showing where it wants to go.
Select E6 and press Delete. The results flow straight back.
Now the at sign. In I2, type equals, at sign, B2 to B11, and press Return. The at sign means give me just one value, the one in my own row. I2 is in row two, so it returns B2.

Fill it down to I11 with Command D. Each cell returns the unit figure from its own row. You'll mostly see the at sign when you open old files, where Excel adds it to keep old formulas working the same way.

acts.h: Select I2:I11 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Prove it's live. Change the units for Ceiling Fan in B10 to 8. The revenue and total update instantly.
A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Dynamic arrays need Microsoft 365 (or Excel 2021+) on Mac.
In Excel 2019 the same formula returns one value, or needs ⌘ + Shift + Return to enter as an old array formula.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• A formula can return many results that spill into neighbouring cells
• E2# refers to the whole spill range, whatever its size
• #SPILL! means something is in the way; @ returns one value from your row

steps.say: Your turn. In K2, write one formula that shows the price including eighteen percent GST for every product, then total it in L2 with a hash reference.

acts.t:
Challenge
K2: =C2:C11*1.18      L2: =SUM(K2#)
Then type something in K5 to see #SPILL!, and delete it.
Answer: sheet S09-01 Done, K2 and L2

lessons.title: UNIQUE, SORT and SORTBY
lessons.mac:
UNIQUE, SORT and SORTBY need Microsoft 365 or Excel 2021+ on Mac.
They work the same in Excel for the web.

steps.say: From twenty sales rows, three formulas build a sorted customer list, a total for each salesperson, and a leaderboard with the top seller first. Add a sale and all of it updates.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. UNIQUE: each value once
2. SORT: sort a list or table by formula
3. SORTBY: sort one list by another, for a leaderboard

Practice sheet: S09-02

steps.say: UNIQUE removes repeats. SORT sorts by one of its own columns. SORTBY sorts by a different list, such as names sorted by their totals.

acts.t:
UNIQUE(array, [by_col], [exactly_once])
SORT(array, [sort_index], [sort_order], [by_col])     sort_order: 1 A-Z, -1 Z-A
SORTBY(array, by_array1, [sort_order1], …)

exactly_once = TRUE lists values that appear only once

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Customers repeat, because most bought more than once.
Here's the common mistake first. In F2, type equals UNIQUE, open bracket, A1 to A21, and press Return.
The heading Customer has crept into the list, because we included row one. Retype it in F2 as equals SORT, open bracket, UNIQUE of A2 to A21, close both and press Return.
Each customer once, in alphabetical order. Now salesperson totals. In H2, type equals UNIQUE of C2 to C21 and press Return.
In I2, type equals SUMIFS, open bracket, D2 to D21, comma, C2 to C21, comma, then H2 hash. One SUMIFS spills a total for every name.
Now the leaderboard. In K2, type equals SORTBY, open bracket, H2 hash, comma, I2 hash, comma, minus 1. Close and press Return. Names sorted by their totals, highest first.
In L2, show the totals in the same order. Type equals SORT, open bracket, I2 hash, comma, comma, minus 1. Close and press Return.
Rahul Wankhede leads. Now change the first sale in D2 to 9,99,000 rupees and watch the totals and the leaderboard reorder.
One more trick.

acts.t:
Pro tip
=SORT(A2:D21, 4, -1) sorts the whole table by Sales, largest first.
=SORTBY(A2:D21, C2:C21, 1, D2:D21, -1) sorts by Salesperson, then Sales.
The source data never moves.

steps.say: A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
UNIQUE, SORT and SORTBY need Microsoft 365 or Excel 2021+ on Mac.
They work the same in Excel for the web.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• UNIQUE lists each value once; leave the heading out of the range
• SORT sorts by its own column; SORTBY sorts by another list
• Spill references like H2# feed one dynamic formula into the next

steps.say: Your turn. In N2, list the customers who bought exactly once, using the third argument of UNIQUE. The answer is on the S09-02 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In N2, list customers who appear exactly once.
Hint: =UNIQUE(A2:A21, , TRUE)
Answer: sheet S09-02 Done, cell N2

lessons.title: FILTER with one or many conditions
lessons.mac:
FILTER needs Microsoft 365 or Excel 2021+ on Mac.
To sort the result, wrap it: =SORT(FILTER(…), 6, -1) puts the biggest amount first.

steps.say: Type a region and a minimum amount in the yellow cells, and this report lists every matching order with one formula. No filter buttons, no copying, and it updates the moment the data changes.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. FILTER with one condition
2. AND and OR conditions
3. A friendly message when nothing matches

Practice sheet: S09-03

steps.say: FILTER returns the rows of a range where a test is TRUE. Multiply tests for AND. Add them for OR. Always put the tests in brackets.

acts.t:
FILTER(array, include, [if_empty])
array: the rows to return (no headings)
include: a TRUE/FALSE test the same height, e.g. C2:C21=I1
if_empty: what to show when nothing matches

AND: (test1)*(test2)      OR: (test1)+(test2)

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Twenty orders, and the inputs are in I1 and I2. First the headings. In H4, type equals A1 colon F1 and press Return.
In H5, type equals FILTER, open bracket, A2 to F21, comma. That's the data without headings.
The include test is C2 to C21 equals I1, the chosen region. Close the bracket and press Return. Every West order appears.
Here's the common mistake. Type Central in I1. There are no Central orders, so FILTER returns hash CALC, which means an empty result.
Fix it with the third argument. Retype H5 as equals FILTER, A2 to F21, comma, C2 to C21 equals I1, comma, No orders in quotes. Press Return.
Now a friendly message instead of an error. Type West back in I1.
Now AND. Retype H5 with the include test in two brackets: C2 to C21 equals I1, then a star, then F2 to F21 greater than or equal to I2.
Press Return. Only West orders of fifty thousand rupees or more remain. The star works because TRUE times TRUE is one, and anything times FALSE is zero.
Now the live report. Change I1 to South. The list rebuilds itself.
For OR, add the tests instead of multiplying them. A row is kept if either test is true.

acts.t:
OR conditions
=FILTER(A2:F21, (C2:C21="North")+(C2:C21="South"), "No orders")
North OR South

Combine both: ((C2:C21="North")+(C2:C21="South"))*(F2:F21>=50000)

steps.say: A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
FILTER needs Microsoft 365 or Excel 2021+ on Mac.
To sort the result, wrap it: =SORT(FILTER(…), 6, -1) puts the biggest amount first.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• FILTER(data, test, "message") returns every matching row
• (test1)*(test2) is AND; (test1)+(test2) is OR
• Point the tests at input cells for a report that updates itself

steps.say: Your turn. In H18, list every Electronics or Furniture order with one FILTER. The answer is on the S09-03 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In H18, list orders where Category is Electronics OR Furniture.
Hint: (D2:D21="Electronics")+(D2:D21="Furniture")
Answer: sheet S09-03 Done, cell H18

lessons.title: SEQUENCE and RANDARRAY
learn: Number lists, calendars and EMI schedules
lessons.mac:
Paste values: ⌘ + Shift + V on current Excel for Mac,
or ⌃ + ⌘ + V and choose Values.
RANDBETWEEN gives one random number; RANDARRAY gives a whole block.

steps.say: Everything in yellow here comes from SEQUENCE: serial numbers, invoice numbers, a November calendar and a twelve-month EMI schedule. The random sales column comes from RANDARRAY, handy for practice data.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. SEQUENCE for number lists, invoice numbers and calendars
2. An EMI schedule that sizes itself
3. RANDARRAY for sample data, and how to freeze it

Practice sheet: S09-04

steps.say: SEQUENCE makes a grid of numbers. You give it rows, columns, a start and a step. RANDARRAY makes random numbers between a minimum and a maximum.

acts.t:
SEQUENCE(rows, [columns], [start], [step])
=SEQUENCE(10)   1 to 10 down a column
=SEQUENCE(5, 7, DATE(2026,10,26))   a 5-week calendar grid

RANDARRAY([rows], [columns], [min], [max], [whole_number])
TRUE = whole numbers only

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. In A2, type equals SEQUENCE, open bracket, 10. Close and press Return. One to ten.
Invoice numbers next. In B2, type equals, INV dash in quotes, ampersand, TEXT, open bracket, SEQUENCE of 10 comma 1 comma 101. Then comma, four zeros in quotes, close and press Return.

INV dash zero one zero one to zero one one zero. Now a calendar. In D2, type equals SEQUENCE, open bracket, 5 rows, comma, 7 columns, comma, then DATE of 2026, 10, 26, the Monday before November starts.
Press Return. The cells are formatted to show just the day, so you get a five-week calendar grid.
Now the EMI schedule. The loan is five lakh at nine percent for twelve months. In B17, type equals PMT, open bracket, B15 divided by 12, comma, B16, comma, minus B14. Close and press Return.
In A20, type equals SEQUENCE of B16 and press Return. Twelve month numbers.
In B20, the due dates: equals EDATE, open bracket, DATE of 2026, 5, 5, comma, A20 hash minus 1. Close and press Return.
In C20, interest each month: equals IPMT, open bracket, B15 divided by 12, comma, A20 hash, comma, B16, comma, minus B14. Close and press Return.
In D20, the same arguments with PPMT for the principal part. Interest falls and principal rises every month.
Change the months in B16 to 24. The schedule grows to twenty-four rows by itself. Then put it back to 12.
Now RANDARRAY. In L2, type equals RANDARRAY, open bracket, 10, comma, 1, comma, 10000, comma, 99999, comma, TRUE. Close and press Return.
Here's the common mistake. Random numbers change every time anything recalculates. Type anything in a cell, say 1 in P1, and the sales figures all change. Sample data that keeps moving is no use.
To freeze them, select L2 to L11, copy with Command C, and paste values with Command Shift V. Now they're plain numbers.
A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Paste values: ⌘ + Shift + V on current Excel for Mac,
or ⌃ + ⌘ + V and choose Values.
RANDBETWEEN gives one random number; RANDARRAY gives a whole block.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• SEQUENCE(rows, columns, start, step) builds lists, grids and calendars
• Feed it a cell (B16) and schedules resize themselves
• RANDARRAY makes practice data; paste as values to freeze it

steps.say: Your turn. In N2, list the first day of each month of the financial year, April 2026 to March 2027, with one formula. The answer is on the S09-04 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In N2, list 01-Apr-2026 to 01-Mar-2027.
Hint: =EDATE(DATE(2026,4,1), SEQUENCE(12, 1, 0))
Answer: sheet S09-04 Done, cell N2

lessons.title: TAKE, DROP and EXPAND
lessons.mac:
TAKE, DROP and EXPAND need Microsoft 365 on Mac or the web.
They are not in Excel 2021 or 2024 perpetual versions.

steps.say: These small reports are cut from bigger lists by formula: the top five salespeople, the last three months, the second quarter, and a block padded to a fixed size.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. TAKE: keep rows from the top or bottom
2. DROP: remove rows from the top or bottom
3. EXPAND: pad an array to a fixed size

Practice sheet: S09-05

steps.say: TAKE keeps a number of rows, DROP removes them. A positive number works from the top, a negative number from the bottom. EXPAND adds rows or columns and fills them with whatever you choose.

acts.t:
TAKE(array, rows, [columns])      TAKE(x, 5) first 5;  TAKE(x, -3) last 3
DROP(array, rows, [columns])      DROP(x, 1) everything except the first row
EXPAND(array, rows, [columns], [pad_with])

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Twenty salespeople on the left, twelve months on the right. Here's the common mistake first. In E2, type equals TAKE, open bracket, A2 to C21, comma, 5. Press Return.
That's just the first five rows of the list, not the top five. TAKE doesn't sort. Retype E2 as equals TAKE, open bracket, SORT of A2 to C21, comma, 3, comma, minus 1, then comma, 5.
Press Return. Now it's the real top five, led by Meera Joshi. Sort first, then take.
Last three months. In E10, type equals TAKE, open bracket, I2 to J13, comma, minus 3. Close and press Return. January, February and March.

Now the second quarter, July to September. Take the first six months, then drop the first three. In E15, type equals DROP, open bracket, TAKE of I2 to J13 comma 6, then comma 3. Close and press Return.
Finally EXPAND. In E20, type equals EXPAND, open bracket, E10 hash, comma, 4 rows, comma, 2 columns, comma, a dash in quotes. Close and press Return.
The three months plus a fourth row of dashes. EXPAND is useful when you stack blocks that must line up, or want a fixed-size area on a report.
Make Divya Menon the top seller: in C11, type 9,90,000 and press Return. The top five reorders.
A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
TAKE, DROP and EXPAND need Microsoft 365 on Mac or the web.
They are not in Excel 2021 or 2024 perpetual versions.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• TAKE(x, n) first n rows, TAKE(x, -n) last n rows
• DROP removes rows; combine TAKE and DROP to slice the middle
• Sort before you TAKE a 'top 5'; EXPAND pads to a fixed size

steps.say: Your turn. In L2, show the bottom three salespeople by sales with one formula. The answer is on the S09-05 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In L2, list the 3 salespeople with the lowest sales.
Hint: =TAKE(SORT(A2:C21, 3, -1), -3)
Answer: sheet S09-05 Done, cell L2

lessons.title: VSTACK, HSTACK, TOCOL, TOROW, WRAPROWS, WRAPCOLS
learn: Combine monthly sheets into one list
lessons.mac:
These functions need Microsoft 365 on Mac or the web.
3-D references (Apr26:Jun26!A2:C6) work on Mac too; keep the month sheets next to each other.

steps.say: The list in columns A to C is three monthly sheets stacked into one by a single formula. On the right, a shift roster is reshaped into a single column, then into rows of four and columns of six, all without copying a cell.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. VSTACK and HSTACK: join arrays down or across
2. Stack monthly sheets with one formula
3. TOCOL, TOROW, WRAPROWS and WRAPCOLS: reshape a block

Practice sheet: S09-06, plus sheets Apr26, May26, Jun26

steps.say: VSTACK puts arrays one under another. HSTACK puts them side by side. TOCOL and TOROW flatten a block into one column or row. WRAPROWS and WRAPCOLS do the opposite.

acts.t:
VSTACK(array1, [array2], …)       HSTACK(array1, [array2], …)
TOCOL(array, [ignore], [scan_by_column])   ignore 1 = skip blanks
TOROW(array, [ignore], [scan_by_column])
WRAPROWS(vector, wrap_count, [pad_with])   WRAPCOLS(vector, wrap_count, [pad_with])

steps.say: Each month sheet has the same layout: Date, Customer and Amount in A1 to C6.
On S09-06, click A1. Type equals VSTACK, open bracket, Apr26 exclamation A1 to C1. That's the heading row, taken once.
Then Apr26 colon Jun26 exclamation A2 to C6. That's a 3-D reference: the same range on every sheet from April to June. Close and press Return.
Fifteen rows from three sheets, under one heading. Add a sheet between Apr26 and Jun26, and it joins automatically.
Now HSTACK. In E1, type equals HSTACK, open bracket, Grand total in quotes, comma, SUM of Apr26 colon Jun26 exclamation C2 to C6. Close both and press Return.
A label and its total, side by side, from one formula. Now the roster in H4 to J7. Here's the common mistake. In H11, type equals TOCOL, open bracket, H4 to J7, and press Return.
Twelve rows, and the last is a zero, because the empty cell in J7 came through as zero. Retype it with comma 1, which tells TOCOL to ignore blanks.
Eleven names in one column. Now wrap them into rows of four. In L4, type equals WRAPROWS, open bracket, H11 hash, comma, 4, comma, empty quotes. Close and press Return.

The empty quotes fill the gap at the end instead of showing an error. WRAPCOLS works down the columns. In L10, type equals WRAPCOLS, open bracket, H11 hash, comma, 6, comma, empty quotes, and press Return.
Last, TOROW. In L19, type equals TOROW, open bracket, H4 to H7, and press Return. The first column of the roster now runs across.
One more mistake to watch for when stacking.

acts.t:
Watch out
VSTACK of arrays with different widths pads the gaps with #N/A:
=VSTACK(Apr26!A2:C6, May26!A2:B6)  → column C shows #N/A for May
Keep widths equal, or wrap in IFNA(…, "")

steps.say: A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
These functions need Microsoft 365 on Mac or the web.
3-D references (Apr26:Jun26!A2:C6) work on Mac too; keep the month sheets next to each other.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• VSTACK(header, Apr26:Jun26!A2:C6) combines monthly sheets in one formula
• HSTACK joins side by side
• TOCOL(x, 1) flattens and skips blanks; WRAPROWS and WRAPCOLS rebuild a grid

steps.say: Your turn. In H24, list every customer from the three months exactly once, using UNIQUE around a VSTACK. The answer is on the S09-06 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In H24, list each customer from Apr26, May26 and Jun26 once.
Hint: =UNIQUE(VSTACK(Apr26:Jun26!B2:B6))
Answer: sheet S09-06 Done, cell H24

lessons.title: GROUPBY, PIVOTBY and PERCENTOF
learn: When to use them instead of a PivotTable
lessons.mac:
GROUPBY, PIVOTBY and PERCENTOF need a current Microsoft 365 build on Mac.
If you see #NAME?, update Excel: Help > Check for Updates.

steps.say: These summaries look like PivotTables, but each one is a single formula. Sales by region with a total, each region's share of the total, and a region by category grid. They update the moment the data changes, with no Refresh button.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. GROUPBY: one-formula summary by rows
2. PIVOTBY: rows and columns, like a pivot
3. PERCENTOF: share of total

Practice sheet: S09-07

steps.say: GROUPBY needs three things: what to group by, what to add up, and how. PIVOTBY adds a second field across the top. The function argument is a name like SUM or AVERAGE, written without quotes or brackets.

acts.t:
GROUPBY(row_fields, values, function, [field_headers], [total_depth], [sort_order], [filter_array], [field_relationship])
PIVOTBY(row_fields, col_fields, values, function, …)
PERCENTOF(data_subset, data_all)

function: SUM, AVERAGE, COUNTA, MAX, PERCENTOF …   sort_order: 2 = by 2nd column, -2 = descending

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Thirty sales with date, region, category, salesperson and amount.
Here's the common mistake first. In G2, type equals GROUPBY, open bracket, B2 to B31, comma, E2 to E31, comma, SUM in quotes. Close and press Return.
Hash VALUE. The function argument isn't text. Retype it with SUM and no quotes.
Four regions in alphabetical order, each with its total, and a grand total at the bottom. Now sort it by sales, biggest first.
Retype G2, adding three commas and minus 2 at the end. The sort order argument means sort by the second column, descending. The three commas skip headers and totals, which keep their defaults.
North is now at the top. Next, the share of each region. In J2, type equals GROUPBY, open bracket, B2 to B31, comma, E2 to E31, comma, PERCENTOF. Close and press Return.
Each region's percentage of the total, adding up to one hundred percent.
Now PIVOTBY. In G10, type equals PIVOTBY, open bracket, B2 to B31 for the rows, comma, C2 to C31 for the columns, comma, E2 to E31, comma, SUM. Close and press Return.
Regions down the side, categories across the top, totals on both edges. Now change the first sale in E2 to 5,00,000 rupees. Every summary updates instantly.
So when should you use these instead of a PivotTable?

acts.t:
Formula or PivotTable?
GROUPBY / PIVOTBY: update instantly, can feed other formulas, easy to filter with a formula
PivotTable: drag-and-drop exploration, slicers, grouping dates, works for big data
Neither needs the source sorted.

steps.say: A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
GROUPBY, PIVOTBY and PERCENTOF need a current Microsoft 365 build on Mac.
If you see #NAME?, update Excel: Help > Check for Updates.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• GROUPBY(group, values, SUM) gives a summary with a total in one formula
• PIVOTBY adds a column field, like a PivotTable
• PERCENTOF gives each group's share; write functions without quotes

steps.say: Your turn. In G18, show the average sale for each salesperson with GROUPBY and AVERAGE. The answer is on the S09-07 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In G18, average Sales for each Salesperson.
Hint: =GROUPBY(D2:D31, E2:E31, AVERAGE)
Answer: sheet S09-07 Done, cell G18

lessons.title: TRIMRANGE and dot references
lessons.mac:
Trim references and TRIMRANGE need a current Microsoft 365 build on Mac or the web.
On older versions, A:.A is a formula error. Update via Help > Check for Updates.

steps.say: This collections log gets new rows every day. The formulas on the right point at a thousand rows, yet they return only the rows that have data, with no trailing zeros. Add a row and they pick it up.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. Why B2:B1000 returns hundreds of zeros
2. The dot reference B2:.B1000 and TRIMRANGE
3. Whole-column references that stay fast

Practice sheet: S09-08

steps.say: A dot next to the colon trims empty rows from that end of the range. B2 colon dot B1000 trims the empty rows at the bottom. TRIMRANGE does the same, as a function.

acts.t:
Trim references
B2:.B1000   trim empty rows at the end (most common)
B2.:B1000   trim empty rows at the start
B2.:.B1000  trim both
A:.A   a whole column, trimmed

TRIMRANGE(range, [trim_rows], [trim_cols])   trim_rows: 0 none, 1 leading, 2 trailing, 3 both

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet, fourteen collection entries. Here's the common mistake. In E2, type equals B2 colon B1000 and press Return.
It spills nine hundred and ninety-nine rows, and every empty row becomes a zero. Press Command Down Arrow to see how far it goes.
Go back to E2. Retype it with a dot after the colon: equals B2 colon dot B1000. Press Return.
Just the fourteen branches, no zeros. Now a summary. In G2, type equals UNIQUE, open bracket, B2 colon dot B1000. Close and press Return.
Without the dot, UNIQUE would add a zero for all the blanks. In H2, type equals SUMIFS, open bracket, C colon C, comma, B colon B, comma, G2 hash. Close and press Return.
SUMIFS on whole columns is fine, because it ignores blanks. Now TRIMRANGE. In J2, type equals ROWS, open bracket, TRIMRANGE of B2 to B1000. Close and press Return. Fourteen rows of data.
Now add a new entry. In B16, type Kolhapur, press Tab, type 38500 and press Return.
The branch list, the summary and the row count all grow. Kolhapur appears with its total, and nothing had to be re-pointed.
When should you use which?

acts.t:
Which one?
B2:.B1000 or A:.A   quick to type, everyday use
TRIMRANGE(range, …)   when you need leading or trailing only, or columns too
Excel Tables   still best for data people type into
Trim refs don't remove blank rows in the MIDDLE of data

steps.say: A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Trim references and TRIMRANGE need a current Microsoft 365 build on Mac or the web.
On older versions, A:.A is a formula error. Update via Help > Check for Updates.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• B2:B1000 in an array formula returns zeros for every empty row
• B2:.B1000 and TRIMRANGE trim the empty rows at the end
• Formulas built on trimmed ranges grow as rows are added

steps.say: Your turn. In L2, show the last three entries of the whole log, all three columns, using TAKE with a trimmed range. The answer is on the S09-08 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In L2, show the last 3 rows of A:C.
Hint: =TAKE(A2:.C1000, -3)
Answer: sheet S09-08 Done, cell L2

lessons.title: LET: readable formulas
learn: Name parts of a long GST formula
lessons.mac:
LET needs Microsoft 365 or Excel 2021+ on Mac.
To make a long formula readable, press ⌃ + ⌥ + Return for a new line inside the formula bar.

steps.say: Column F and column G give the same totals. F repeats the same calculation four times and is hard to check. G uses LET to name each step, gross, net and GST, so anyone can read it.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. Name the parts of a long GST formula with LET
2. Debug a LET formula one step at a time
3. Naming rules to avoid errors

Practice sheet: S09-09

steps.say: LET works in pairs. A name, then its value, as many pairs as you like, and finally the calculation that uses those names. Each part is worked out once, which also makes the formula faster.

acts.t:
LET(name1, value1, [name2, value2, …], calculation)

=LET(gross, B2*C2,
     net,   gross*(1-D2),
     gst,   net*E2,
     net+gst)
Names: start with a letter, no spaces, not like a cell address (GST1, Q1, R, C)

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Click F2 and look at the formula bar. B2 times C2 appears four times. One typo and the total is wrong.
In G2, type equals LET, open bracket. First pair: gross, comma, B2 times C2, comma.
Second pair: net, comma, gross times, open bracket, 1 minus D2, close bracket, comma. Net uses the name gross we just made.
Third pair: gst, comma, net times E2, comma.
Last comes the calculation: net plus gst. Close the bracket and press Return. Same total as column F.
Fill it down to G11 with Command D.

acts.h: Select G2:G11 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Here's the common mistake. In G3, type equals LET, open bracket, gst1, comma, B3 times C3, comma, gst1. Close and press Return.
Excel refuses, because GST1 is a real cell address, column GST, row one. Click OK and press Escape. Use names that can't be mistaken for cells.
Fill G2 down again with Command D so every row uses the good formula.

acts.h: Select G2:G11 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: Here's how to debug a LET formula. Swap the final calculation for any name, and the cell shows that step.

acts.t:
Pro tip: debug step by step
Change the last argument to see each stage:
=LET(gross,B2*C2, net,gross*(1-D2), gst,net*E2, gross)   → shows gross
… , net)   → shows net      … , gst)   → shows GST
Put net+gst back when you're done

steps.say: Prove it's live. Change the laptop discount in D3 to 10 percent. The LET total updates.
A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
LET needs Microsoft 365 or Excel 2021+ on Mac.
To make a long formula readable, press ⌃ + ⌥ + Return for a new line inside the formula bar.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• LET(name, value, …, calculation) names each step
• Each step is calculated once: shorter, faster, easier to check
• Avoid names that look like cell addresses, such as GST1

steps.say: Your turn. In H2, use LET to return just the GST amount, rounded to two decimals, then fill it down. The answer is on the S09-09 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In H2:H11, return only the GST amount, rounded to 2 decimals.
Hint: =LET(gross, B2*C2, net, gross*(1-D2), ROUND(net*E2, 2))
Answer: sheet S09-09 Done, column H

lessons.title: LAMBDA and its helpers
learn: BYROW, BYCOL, MAP, REDUCE, SCAN, MAKEARRAY
lessons.mac:
LAMBDA and its helpers need Microsoft 365 on Mac or the web.
Names you define travel with the workbook, so colleagues can use GSTINCL too.
Formulas > Name Manager lists and edits them.

steps.say: Column F uses a function that doesn't come with Excel. GSTINCL is our own, made with LAMBDA and saved as a name. The other columns use LAMBDA helpers: MAP, SCAN, REDUCE, BYROW, BYCOL and MAKEARRAY.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. Write a LAMBDA and test it in a cell
2. Save it as your own function, GSTINCL
3. The helpers: MAP, SCAN, REDUCE, BYROW, BYCOL, MAKEARRAY

Practice sheet: S09-10

steps.say: LAMBDA lists the inputs first and the calculation last. On its own it does nothing. You give it values in a second pair of brackets, or save it in the Name Manager and call it by name.

acts.t:
LAMBDA([parameter1, parameter2, …], calculation)
=LAMBDA(amt, rate, amt*(1+rate))(B2, C2)   test it in a cell
Formulas > Define Name: GSTINCL = LAMBDA(amt, rate, amt*(1+rate))
=GSTINCL(B2, C2)

Parameter names: not R, C or anything like a cell address

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Amounts in column B and GST rates in column C. Here's the common mistake first. In E2, type equals LAMBDA, open bracket, amt, comma, rate, comma, amt times, open bracket, 1 plus rate. Close both and press Return.
Hash CALC. We wrote a function but never gave it any values. Retype it and add B2 comma C2 in a second pair of brackets at the end.
Sixty-nine thousand five hundred and two rupees, the laptop with GST. The LAMBDA works, so let's save it. On the Formulas tab, click Define Name.
Name: GSTINCL. In Refers to, type equals LAMBDA, amt, rate, amt times 1 plus rate, without the test values. Click OK.
In F2, type equals GSTINCL, open bracket, B2 to B11, comma, C2 to C11. Close and press Return. Our own function, spilling ten answers.
Now MAP, which runs a LAMBDA on each item. In G2, type equals MAP, open bracket, B2 to B11, comma, C2 to C11, comma, LAMBDA of amt, rate, then IF rate equals zero, Exempt, otherwise amt times rate.
Press Return. GST amounts, with Exempt for the zero-rated items such as vegetables and books.
SCAN keeps a running result. In H2, type equals SCAN, open bracket, zero, comma, B2 to B11, comma, LAMBDA of acc, v, acc plus v. Close and press Return. A running total.
REDUCE does the same but returns only the final answer. In I2, type the same formula with REDUCE instead of SCAN, and press Return.
Now BYROW. The branch table below is in lakh. In F15, type equals BYROW, open bracket, B15 to E19, comma, LAMBDA of br, SUM of br. Close and press Return. One total per branch.
BYCOL works down each column. In B20, type equals BYCOL, open bracket, B15 to E19, comma, LAMBDA of qtr, MAX of qtr. Close and press Return. The best branch figure in each quarter.
Last, MAKEARRAY builds a grid from row and column numbers. In H15, type equals MAKEARRAY, open bracket, 3, comma, 4, comma, LAMBDA of i, j, i times j. Close and press Return.
Change the laptop amount in B2 to 62,000. GSTINCL, MAP, SCAN and REDUCE all update.
A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
LAMBDA and its helpers need Microsoft 365 on Mac or the web.
Names you define travel with the workbook, so colleagues can use GSTINCL too.
Formulas > Name Manager lists and edits them.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• LAMBDA(inputs, calculation); test it with (values) on the end
• Save it with Define Name to get your own function
• MAP per item, SCAN running, REDUCE final, BYROW / BYCOL per row or column, MAKEARRAY builds a grid

steps.say: Your turn. In H21, use MAP to round every GSTINCL result in F2 hash to the nearest ten rupees. The answer is on the S09-10 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In H21, round each value of F2# to the nearest ₹10.
Hint: =MAP(F2#, LAMBDA(v, ROUND(v, -1)))
Answer: sheet S09-10 Done, cell H21

lessons.title: IMAGE and pictures in cells
lessons.mac:
IMAGE and Place in Cell need Microsoft 365 on Mac or the web.
Select a picture cell and the formula bar shows its IMAGE formula.
Images come from the web, so files may open slowly offline.

steps.say: This product list shows a photo inside each cell, pulled from a web link with the IMAGE function. On the right, pick a product and its price and photo appear, like a small catalogue card.
Here's the plan.

acts.t:
In this lesson
1. IMAGE: a picture from a web address, inside a cell
2. Sizing options
3. Look up a picture with XLOOKUP, and Place in Cell for your own files

Practice sheet: S09-11

steps.say: IMAGE needs a direct link to a picture file that starts with https. The picture lives in the cell, so it moves, sorts and filters with your data.

acts.t:
IMAGE(source, [alt_text], [sizing], [height], [width])
source: https link to a .jpg, .png, .gif, .bmp, .tiff, .ico or .webp file
alt_text: description for screen readers
sizing: 0 fit (default), 1 fill, 2 original size, 3 custom height and width

steps.say: Here's the practice sheet. Each product has a link to its photo in column C.
In D2, type equals IMAGE, open bracket, C2 for the link, comma, A2 as the alt text. Close and press Return.
The masala chai photo appears inside the cell. Fill it down to D6 with Command D.

acts.h: Select D2:D6 and fill down with ⌘ + D

steps.say: If Excel shows a yellow bar about linked images, click to enable them. Excel only downloads pictures you allow.

acts.t:
Note
If a security bar says linked images are blocked, enable them for this workbook.
Pictures load from the internet, so you need a connection the first time.

steps.say: Here's the common mistake. In D7, type equals IMAGE, with a link to the web page about the mango, not the picture file itself. Press Return.
An error. That link opens a web page, not an image file. Right-click the picture on the page and copy the image address instead. Press Delete to clear D7.
Now the catalogue card. In H2, type equals XLOOKUP, open bracket, H1, comma, A2 to A6, comma, B2 to B6. Close and press Return. Nine hundred and fifty rupees.
In H3, the same lookup but return D2 to D6, the photos. Press Return. XLOOKUP returns the picture itself.
Type Coorg Coffee Beans, open bracket, 1 kg, close bracket, in H1. The price and photo switch.

acts.h: Type Coorg Coffee Beans (1 kg) and press Return

steps.say: For your own pictures, there's no link. Use Place in Cell.

acts.t:
Pictures from your Mac
Insert > Pictures > Place in Cell > This Device (web)
Excel for Mac: Insert > Pictures > Place in Cell > Picture from File
Already have a floating picture? Select it, then Place in Cell (right-click menu)
Pictures in cells sort and filter with their rows

steps.say: A Mac note.

acts.t:
Mac corner
IMAGE and Place in Cell need Microsoft 365 on Mac or the web.
Select a picture cell and the formula bar shows its IMAGE formula.
Images come from the web, so files may open slowly offline.

steps.say: Here's the recap.

acts.t:
Recap
• =IMAGE(link, alt text) puts a web picture in a cell
• The link must point to the image file, starting with https
• XLOOKUP can return a picture; Place in Cell handles your own files

steps.say: Your turn. In E2 to E6, show small thumbnails, forty by forty pixels, using sizing option 3. The answer is on the S09-11 Done sheet.

acts.t:
Challenge
In E2:E6, show 40 × 40 pixel thumbnails.
Hint: =IMAGE(C2, A2, 3, 40, 40)
Answer: sheet S09-11 Done, column E
